  "required_fixes": [
    "F1 (high) — crates/desktop-core/src/harness/session.rs:1155 and crates/desktop-core/src/authority/harness_tools.rs:338-391,439-450: host tools lack a turn-scoped lifetime. on_tool_call still accepts the matching turn after interrupt_wanted is set; the sink detaches jobs without cancellation, and run checks harness_live separately from the later management/scan admission. Interrupt clears only reply bookkeeping, while the tenant ContextRef can remain valid after Stop, End, or a project/access change. Consequently old-turn scans/reads or proposal staging can begin or continue after withdrawal. ToolResult also identifies only an engine RequestId, which can be reused after renewal restarts. Bind admission, outstanding operations and results to an engine/run/turn lease; stop admitting after interruption, cancel work still queued, and discard stale completions without claiming rollback for already-dispatched work. Acceptance: barrier-controlled tools interrupted before admission/while queued produce no later remote request or proposal; late results cannot satisfy a new turn or restarted engine request with a reused ID.",
    "F2 (high) — crates/desktop-core/src/authority/harness_tools.rs:392, crates/desktop-core/src/harness/tools.rs:374-405, and crates/desktop-core/src/management.rs:377,534,1482: the new model-result scrubber does not traverse the actual management payload. ManagementPage.items and several detail/session fields are JSON text strings. serde_json::to_value(result) preserves those strings, and scrub ignores strings. The earlier management redactor removes only its exact ten field names, so an authorization field or case variant preserved in an item's unknown fields bypasses C21's stronger credential filter and reaches the remote model. Convert known JSON-bearing result fields into a structured, model-safe representation before scrubbing/serialization, or enforce an equivalent filter before those fields become strings. Acceptance: a tool exercised through the production management interface receives nested authorization and mixed-case credential canaries in page/detail payloads; none reaches the Gateway tool output, while safe unknown metadata remains usable.",
    "F3 (high) — crates/desktop-core/src/harness/session.rs:1220-1245 and apps/desktop/src/features/harness/decisions-panel.tsx:86-105: approvals can authorize actions whose scope is unavailable to the operator. Commands are irreversibly truncated at 2 KiB before display, with no full-command view, while Allow accepts the original request. File-change approvals are accepted even when the cached filenames are absent; C21-N04's retained native observation actually shows only 'Change files' and no filename. Do not enable approval for missing or hidden execution scope: provide complete, bounded reviewable command/file details, or decline requests whose details cannot be established with the pinned engine. Acceptance: a command with an effect-bearing suffix past the display bound cannot be approved unseen; a real file-change approval names all affected files before Allow is enabled; unavailable metadata fails closed and cancellation runs nothing.",
    "F4 (medium) — crates/desktop-core/src/harness/session.rs:1313-1326 versus packages/desktop-contracts/src/client.ts:1177: updating an existing command/file-change entry bypasses the cumulative transcript limit enforced by push. A command's completion replaces its short started text with command plus output without trimming or evicting entries. An independent in-memory probe of the production parseShellSnapshot accepted a 103-entry started snapshot at 1,047,548 bytes and rejected its completed form at 1,055,750 bytes, although both fit the entry-count and individual-text limits. The entire shell observation/update is then rejected. Enforce the same cumulative byte invariant on replacements as on insertions, with truthful truncation/retention. Acceptance: near-limit command completions and file-change updates remain within the Rust bound and pass the production snapshot validator without suppressing subsequent updates."
  ],
  "blockers": [],
  "evidence_gaps": [
    "C21 explicitly requires T23 offline/reconnect acceptance, but its seven integration scenarios and native driver do not exercise disconnection/reconnection with pending host tools, approvals or proposals. The successful restore-with-no-command-replay test covers a completed online turn, not that boundary. Add scoped evidence for applicable local history/project work while offline, preserved uncertain outcomes, stale approval/review invalidation, and no automatic scan/tool/action resubmission on reconnect; distinguish an explicit retry from replay. Include the delayed/cancelled tool cases in F1."
  ],
  "optional_suggestions": [
    "Return a valid structured truncation envelope for oversized tool results instead of cutting serialized JSON mid-value; the current cut note is explicit but leaves the model with malformed JSON.",
    "Use future tense in the confirmWrite prompt: 'Your sign-in was renewed' is shown before renewal occurs. The integration test correctly establishes zero refreshes until the operator allows continuation."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Independent read-only audits matched all four supplied fingerprints, the 673-entry source inventory and 373 referenced hashes, including run logs/artifacts and the C20 receipt/raw verdict.     "I independently exercised the production TypeScript snapshot validator in memory and recomputed all six workload statistics from retained samples; all recorded workload statistics are within their registered limits. Source and evidence were unchanged at final audit.",
    "Real model, management, Gateway and identity-provider qualification remains C25; signed/notarized installed-package acceptance remains C26. The pinned engine's patch helper fails to write after approval, as disclosed and tested; approved shell writes work.
